        No. 1 Georgia is heading to its sixth consecutive SEC Championship Game after clinching a spot during Saturday night's impressive win at South Carolina.In what most expect to be the last SEC Championship Game with Power Four leagues expected to do away with title games to make room for next year's 24-team playoff, the Bulldogs will face either Texas, Tennessee or Alabama.
SEC's race for second placeTeamRecordWeek 13 OpponentAlabama6-2vs. Auburn, Saturday Tennessee6-2at Vanderbilt, SaturdayTexas6-2at Texas A&M, FridayGoing through various scenarios coming out of Week 12 results, after wins from the Vols, Longhorns and Crimson Tide kept things even, here's where everything stands with one conference game left for each squad:Tennessee clinches bid if ...Vols finish in sole possession of second place at 7-2 after beating Vanderbilt, Texas loses to Texas A&M and Alabama loses to Auburn.Vols finish tied with Alabama in second place at 7-2 after beating Vanderbilt, Texas loses to Texas A&M and Alabama beats Auburn. Tennessee wins head-to-head tiebreaker since it beat the Crimson Tide earlier this season.Texas clinches bid if ...Longhorns beat Texas A&M, Tennessee loses to Vanderbilt and Alabama loses to Auburn.Longhorns beat Texas A&M, Tennessee beats Vanderbilt and Alabama loses to Auburn. Texas wins head-to-head tiebreaker since it beat the Vols earlier this season.Alabama clinches bid if... The Tide beat Auburn, Texas loses to Texas A&M and Tennessee loses to Vanderbilt If Texas and Alabama both win and Tennessee loses. the tiebreaker would come down to records vs. common opponents If Alabama, Tennessee and Texas all win next weekend ...In the event of a three-way tie for second-place at 7-2 in league play behind Georgia, the league would go down the list to its fourth tiebreaker: cumulative SEC winning percentage of each tied team's conference opponents. Alabama was the percentage leader heading into Saturday's games, but that changed to Texas after Missouri beat Kentucky and Oklahoma took out Texas A&M. Should all three teams win next weekend, the outcomes of Ole Miss-Mississippi State and Arkansas-LSU will be significant. 247Sports broke down those four scenario results as follows: Alabama goes if Mississippi State and LSU win; Texas goes if Mississippi State and Arkansas win; Texas goes if Ole Miss and LSU win; Texas goes if Ole Miss and Arkansas win. In other words, odds are slim Alabama will play Georgia in Atlanta.

title: Tomorrow's Top 25 Today: Ohio State, Indiana, UCLA fall in college football rankings amid Big Ten chaos - CBS Sports
description: Projecting the new AP Top 25 poll after Saturday's chaos will cause a shakeup in the college football rankings
body:
Projecting the new AP Top 25 poll after Saturday's chaos will cause a shakeup in the college football rankings
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One read of Saturday's college football schedule suggested we might be in for a sleepy weekend. After all, Week 12 marked the first time since 2009 that there were no games between teams ranked in the AP Top 25 poll (excluding 2020). Some differences with the College Football Playoff rankings did have one such game highlighted on the slate, but the lack of ranked-on-ranked matchups did stand in contrast to some of the seemingly loaded slates in previous weeks. So of course it was Week 12, the week that had some of the least games between ranked teams, that provided one of the biggest shake-ups to the college football rankings we have seen this season. The chaos came in the form of upsets, and the upset bug bit hard on the Big Ten. The conference had five teams in the AP poll last week but saw three of them lose on the road to unranked opponents. Seeing UCLA, Indiana and Ohio State all fall on the same day changed the math for the Big Ten title race and the College Football Playoff picture. We will find out what the selection committee has to say on Tuesday night, but the AP voters could give us a hint as to where all three will land after their projected drops in the rankings. Ohio State may find itself all the way out of the top 25 entirely, which would mark the first time since 2011 that the Buckeyes would be unranked in the AP Top 25 poll (excluding 2020). Falling to No. 16 set Ohio State dangerously close to their previous AP poll low of No. 21, which is where the 2014 team bottomed out before charging back into the CFP picture and eventually winning the national title. Unfortunately, no such path is still available to Ryan Day's squad in 2026, as Ohio State enters its rivalry game against Michigan with a 7-4 record and very little momentum, having lost three of their last four games. 
Trying to sort out the conference title tiebreakers and College Football Playoff conundrums will continue through the week, but after the chaos of Week 12, here's how we think the new AP Top 25 poll will look on Sunday: 1. Georgia (Last week -- 1): A spot in the final SEC Championship Game was clinched on Saturday as Georgia passed its final road test with a win at South Carolina. The Bulldogs were clinical in the 34-6 win, dominating on defense and leaning on the Gamecocks over four quarters to secure a fourth-straight double-digit win.  2. Utah (2): The Utes are currently in action at TCU. 3. Notre Dame (3): On a night when upsets and upset scares littered the top 25 scoreboard, Notre Dame was able to fly under the radar with a business-like approach to winning against SMU to improve to 10-1. 
4. Miami (5): The Hurricanes trailed by two touchdowns early against Virginia Tech but stormed back to hold on for a 28-20 win that clinched their spot in the ACC Championship Game. 5. Tennessee (9): We are projecting a decent jump for Tennessee in the wake of its 27-13 win against LSU. The Vols were underdogs in the eyes of the oddsmakers against the unranked Tigers, but out-executed Lane Kiffin's group before a rocking atmosphere in Neyland Stadium. With a 9-2 record and another strong win, we're projecting AP voters will respect the head-to-head result against Alabama as they re-shuffle the top 10 following Saturday's chaos. 6. Alabama (7): The Crimson Tide rolled in their game against FCS Chattanooga, getting to rest Keelon Russell while also running up the score for the home fans. Backup quarterback Austin Mack totaled five touchdowns in relief (four passing, one rushing), and Alabama improved to 9-2 after the 47-0 win. 
7. Texas (8): It was a great day for a boring blowout win, as Texas fans had limited anxiety during a stressful Saturday for other top-10 teams. The Longhorns led 24-3 at halftime and cruised to a 45-3 win that was highlighted by three total touchdowns from Arch Manning (two passing, one rushing) and noticeable skill position depth for Steve Sarkisian's offense. 8. Wake Forest (10): In a season that has been chaotic and unpredictable compared to weekly expectations, nothing has proven to be more consistent over the last month than Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons are smashing teams in the first half and cruising to double-digit wins against ACC opponents, continuing that trend on Saturday in a 50-29 win at Georgia Tech. 9. Texas Tech (11): The Red Raiders' defense answered the call on the road against in-state foe Baylor, holding the Bears to just 257 yards of offense at 3.62 yards per play. That edge was crucial to overcome three turnovers on offense and helped Texas Tech hold on for a 20-10 win to improve to 10-1 on the year.  
10. UCLA (4): There is a value of aesthetics when it comes to how voters react to UCLA's first loss of the season. The Bruins were slow to make their move up in the rankings until they toppled Oregon, and even last week was ranked behind two other teams with losses despite having a 10-0 record. So yes, the AP voters might have some doubts that will be addressed in their re-ranking of UCLA following the upset loss.    11. BYU (12): The magic of Bear Bachmeier in the short areas proved to be enough for BYU to avoid a misstep on the road and keep their College Football Playoff argument strong. Bachmeier ran for two touchdowns, and Jojo Phillips pulled in the game-winning two-point try in triple overtime, breaking the hearts of the upset-minded Kansas fans in Lawrence.  12. Indiana (6): The Hoosiers are in some real trouble as injuries and close-game fortune have both seemingly turned the other way on the reigning national champions. Curt Cignetti saw more injuries to key starters, even as Josh Hoover returned to the lineup, and Indiana is set to tumble in the rankings with a 9-2 profile that's heavy on win total and lighter on win quality. 
13. Iowa (13): The Hawkeyes won their fourth game in a row, pulling away from Illinois in a 34-17 win to improve to 9-2 overall. Iowa might need some help to make the Big Ten title game, but a win next week against Minnesota could secure an awfully impressive 10-2 season to present to the selection committee at the end of the year. 14. Oregon (14): The Ducks deserve a lot of credit for being able to rally back from a midseason slump, as the team's recent momentum seemed to travel with the team to East Lansing for their Friday night spotlight. Oregon poured on the points late for a 45-7 final score that keeps the Ducks in the conversation as they enter the final week of the regular season with an 8-3 record and a shot at cracking the top 12. 15. Boise State (15): The Broncos are currently in action against San Diego State. 
16. USC (18): Lincoln Riley led the Trojans to a 35-21 win against Maryland to close out the home schedule at the Coliseum and set up a colossal showdown with UCLA next week at the Rose Bowl. USC might not have the exact Big Ten title or College Football Playoff stakes they wanted coming into the year, but the Trojans will be a main character in the final week of conference play for both competitions, and Riley has a chance to score a big win with the fans playing spoiler to the cross-town rivals. 17. Arizona (19): The Wildcats are currently in action at Kansas State. 18. Houston (20): We do not expect Houston to get docked for winning close, 34-31 at West Virginia, but the Cougars' resume strength isn't fantastic when voters are breaking ties on their ballots. Houston is 8-3 but 0-2 against other ranked teams (Utah, Texas Tech), with a top-35 caliber win against Oklahoma State as the highlight of the profile. 19. Louisville (21): Jeff Brohm is in position to finish the season somewhere close to the preseason expectations, with an 8-3 record heading into the rivalry game against Kentucky. Now, how Louisville has arrived at 8-3, with losses in two of the first three ACC games, was not expected. But after a win against Pitt, the Cardinals hold a solid top 25 resume with a chance to bolster that position against Will Stein net weekend in Lexington.  
20. Liberty (22): The Flames were not ranked by the College Football Playoff Selection Committee but did crash the AP voters' top 25 last week. Now at 10-1 after a 45-14 home win against Western Kentucky, Liberty rides the power of that impressive winning percentage to a slight bump up. 21. Florida (23): The Gators did not offer a ton of evidence for continued voter support in a back-and-forth with Vanderbilt that saw both offenses move the ball effectively. Florida finished strong with a score and a fourth-down stop late in the fourth quarter, holding on for a 34-27 win.  22. Oklahoma (NR): A three-touchdown win against Texas A&M should propel the Sooners out of the "Others receiving votes" category and into the top 25. A head-to-head advantage against Ole Miss should help voters place Oklahoma on their ballots who might have had them off last week, since both teams are now 7-4 and the Sooners now have more SEC wins on the season. 
23. Ole Miss (25): The margins were very thin at the cut line for the top 25, with Ole Miss holding the narrowest edge on the teams checking in at No. 26 and No. 27 in voting points. A 59-17 win against FCS Wofford doesn't boost their stock, but losses elsewhere should sharpen the ballot and have Ole Miss safely in the top 25 again. 24. Nebraska (NR): The quality loss Cornhuskers argue a four-loss team worth top 25 consideration after toppling Ohio State on Saturday in Lincoln. Matt Rhule's elusive win against a ranked team reverses the recent trend after close losses to Indiana, Oregon and Washington (by a combined 13 points) had Nebraska underperforming its quality in the conference standings. The entire resume doesn't offer a top of high-end wins aside from Saturday's win against the Buckeyes, but a recency bias could be enough to push Nebraska back into the top 25.  25. Missouri (NR): Welcome back, Missouri, to your spot here in the 20s of the AP Top 25 poll. The Tigers beat Kentucky on Saturday night, bouncing the Wildcats from the rankings and jumping ahead in line among those power conference teams on the cut line of the ballot. Missouri is 7-4 overall with a win against Florida to pair with the Week 12 win against the Wildcats, and if asked to choose between that resume and a two-loss Group of Six team, we project that the strength of schedule edge will win out in the eyes of the AP voters. 
Projected to drop out: No. 16 Ohio State, No. 17 Kentucky, No. 24 Memphis

title: College football winners, losers: Luck runs out for Indiana, Oregon rounding into form - CBS Sports
description: Plus, Ohio State hit a historic low against Nebraska, while Tennessee made a major statement in the College Footb
body:
Plus, Ohio State hit a historic low against Nebraska, while Tennessee made a major statement in the College Football Playoff race
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College football's Week 12 didn't have much to offer on paper. There was only one ranked matchup on the schedule, with most of the top teams instead dodging tough games. As always, the sport delivered. Multiple top 10 teams fell, with the Big Ten taking a particular tumble. No. 4 UCLA's loss to Michigan leaves Utah as the Power Four's only undefeated team. While they ultimately survived, No. 10 BYU also faced a major test at Kansas that went into triple overtime. Ultimately, two of the CFP Top 10 fell and five of the top 25. No. 7 Miami also played a tight game in the night stretch, but kept the dream of a two-bid ACC alive. Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 12 entering the evening slate. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: GeorgiaWe're running out of superlatives to describe Georgia. On a day where many of the nation's best teams went down to the wire, the Bulldogs went on the road and disemboweled Shane Beamer and the No. 21 Gamecocks in a 34-6 victory. 
The Bulldogs threw for 281 yards, rushed for 140 yards and held LaNorris Sellers to only 87 total yards. They scored 31 straight points from the two-minute mark of the third quarter on. Outside of the bizarre loss to Auburn, Georgia has been untouchable. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Ohio StatePlenty of attention will be paid to Ohio State's quarterback injuries after its stunning 31-28 loss against Nebraska, snapping a Cornhuskers' losing streak of 31 straight games against ranked competition. But during a third loss in four games, every single issue that's plagued Ryan Day's squad showed up. The Buckeyes mustered only 76 yards rushing on 22 carries and gave up 176 to the Cornhuskers on the road. The defense completely failed to get off the field, allowing Nebraska to run nearly 20 more plays. Quarterback Luke Fahey actually played fine, throwing for 259 yards and two touchdowns. The passing game just isn't good enough to cover up every other hole anymore. 
Now, Ohio State has its most losses in a season since 2011, an interim-coached group. For all intents and purposes, 2026 Ohio State is the most disappointing Buckeyes squad of the 21st Century. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Wake ForestThe Demon Deacons are absolutely ruthless. Wake Forest finally allowed a first-half touchdown against Georgia Tech after four straight games without one, but they impressed mightily during a 50-29 win over the Yellow Jackets. The final score doesn't do justice to Wake Forest's dominance. The program went up 29-0 and 43-7 early in the second half. They cleared 600 yards and an absurd 15.2 yards per pass attempt. With the dominance, Wake Forest will have a chance to move even higher in the CFP Rankings, especially as teams above them looked shaky. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: IndianaThe Hoosiers' magical run finally came crashing down against Washington, putting the No. 8 Indiana in a precarious position. Indiana shuffled through quarterbacks, but the defense had a disappointing day in a 27-24 loss to Washington, the first two-loss regular season of the Curt Cignetti era. Indiana was playing with fire for much of the season, recording overtime wins against lackluster Michigan and Minnesota squads. But after losing to Washington, the Hoosiers' place in the playoff looks far more tenuous. Indiana only has one ranked win against No. 18 USC, and the Hoosiers' opponents are 23-33 against Power Four competition. Could that knock them all the way down to the edge of the bubble? 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: OregonFor maybe the first time all season, the Ducks look like the squad that was promised. Quarterback Dylan Raiola took to the sky and never looked back, throwing for 234 yards in a 45-7 win against Michigan State, dominated by the highly-rated defense. 
With the win, Oregon has quietly snuck back into the Big Ten title race at 6-2 in conference. The Ducks are still alive in the final week with a tiebreaker coming between Indiana and Iowa. If they get it, could Oregon be the team that no one wants to play in December? 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Penn StateThere's absolutely no explanation for how Penn State lost this game, 25-24 against Rutgers. They led 16-0 in the second quarter and 24-10 in the third. They even led as the clock struck zero, but Antwan Raymond tossed the ball to Ben Black, who somehow made it into the end zone for a touchdown. The home loss was a major embarrassment for Penn State and tamped down excitement after a promising couple of weeks. The Nittany Lions had won three straight, including a 42-14 win over Minnesota last week. Reaching eight wins would have felt promising, but now Campbell's team will have to beat Maryland on the road just to clear .500. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: NebraskaOhio State is deservedly getting more of the attention after the game earlier, but the generational curses broken in Lincoln can't be ignored. Nebraska had lost 31 straight games against ranked competition. Matt Rhule had not beaten a ranked opponent since 2016, while coach at Temple. As the game closed, it felt like Nebraska had to fight fate dragging them down. Ohio State managed to drive 75 yards down the field with ease to cut the lead to one score. But on third-and-five, Anthony Colandrea got six to run out the clock. It's taken years for Rhule to get some of the curses out of the program; hopefully this can be another. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: BYUThe Cougars managed to survive a triple-overtime game against Kansas, but BYU just continues to play with fire. BYU allowed 17 unanswered points through the fourth quarter and overtime before finally getting a few scores in overtime. The Cougars also mustered only three first-half points one week after dropping 21 on Baylor at home. 
Surviving the game at least means the Cougars remain alive in the playoff race, but their historic win over Notre Dame is getting further in their rearview mirror. Despite winning, BYU will likely fall behind Wake Forest in the College Football Playoff Rankings, putting them right on the chopping block. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: TennesseeVols coach Josh Heupel has not gotten enough credit for his job this season. Despite starting quarterback George MacIntyre being hobbled in a 27-13 win over LSU, Heupel pushed all the right buttons. After initially starting Faizon Brandon, Heupel deftly switched between the two passers, ultimately using Brandon as an effective run threat. The defense, of course, came to play against Sam Leavitt. Now, Tennessee is all but assured a spot in the College Football Playoff. 
Heupel's teams are characterized by dynamic offenses and downfield threats. It's a major testament to Heupel's coaching that the Volunteers have managed to reach contention despite inconsistent passing. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Texas A&MThe Aggies have flown under the radar after tanking early in the season, but a 28-7 loss against No. 22 Oklahoma was a nail in the coffin. Texas A&M are already eliminated from bowl eligibility, their first year without a bowl since Jimbo Fisher's 5-7 season in 2022, and only the second time since 2007. This one featured all the hallmarks that have made the season frustrating for Aggies' fans. The run game got only 54 yards on 32 carries against an elite defense. The downfield passing game showed a little promise with 131 yards -- including a 36-yard bomb -- from first-time quarterback Brady Hart. But unless Texas A&M can stun Texas in Week 13, this will go down as perhaps the worst season of the 21st Century. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Louisiana TechThe Bulldogs are quietly having one of the best seasons in college football. Louisiana Tech picked up losses to LSU and Baylor in nonconference play. Since then, they've won eight straight, including a 7-0 mark in Sun Belt play. Louisiana Tech is the only team still undefeated in Sun Belt play, and could play Georgia Southern in consecutive weeks to win their first conference championship since a WAC title in 2011. Sonny Cumbie deserves major credit for kicking down the door of the Sun Belt in the Bulldogs' first year in the league. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: South FloridaThe Bulls have quietly been one of the most disappointing teams in college football this season, limping out to a 6-5 record despite a strong roster spend. A 35-14 loss to FAU laid bare USF's situation. The Owls jumped out to a 28-0 lead early in the third quarter, driving the Bulls into the dirt in a cross-state rivalry game. South Florida was thoroughly outcoached and outclassed by a team without a bowl appearance since 2020. Any hope that Hartline could be a plug-and-play hire is off the table.

body:
Expect some major movement in the new CFP rankings after major chaos within the Big Ten
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Several teams on the College Football Playoff bubble kept their best-case scenarios in play approaching rivalry weekend to end the regular season.For others, it's all about survival — especially in a now uber-chaotic Big Ten.Previously-unbeaten and fourth-ranked UCLA is sure to drop in the CFP rankings after a stunning three-overtime loss at Michigan, one that also cost the Bruins starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach. Making his sixth straight start this fall following a season-ending injury to Nico Iamaleava, Dieffenbach was carted off in the first overtime before being relieved by Madden Iamaleava, UCLA's emergency third option.Three years ago, the CFP selection committee left unbeaten Florida State out of the final four-team bracket after the Seminoles lost quarterback Jordan Travis to a serious injury before winning the ACC Championship Game.
Could the Bruins suffer a similar fate — at least in terms of seeding — in the final year of the 12-team era?Defending national champion and eighth-ranked Indiana's overtime loss at Washington cratered the Hoosiers' shot at getting back to the Big Ten Championship and now, Curt Cignetti's squad needs assistance.No. 10 BYU staved off an upset bid at Kansas with a double-overtime win, while No. 14 Ohio State wasn't so lucky after playing itself off the bubble following a loss at Nebraska -- the Huskers' first win under Matt Rhule over a ranked opponent after 10 previous losses.
No. 13 Oregon opened Week 12 with its fourth straight win, disposing of Michigan State, 45-7, for style points on Friday night prior to No. 11 Wake Forest's impressive 50-29 victory Saturday afternoon in Atlanta against Georgia Tech. Those are two teams that look the part, with long winning streaks down the stretch.CFP bubble after Saturday's gamesCurrent CFP rankingWeek 12 resultsBYUNo. 10Win at Kansas, 31-29 (3OT)Wake Forest No. 11Win at Georgia Tech, 50-29Texas TechNo. 12Win at Baylor, 20-10OregonNo. 13Win at Michigan State, 45-7 (Friday)Ohio StateNo. 14Lost at Nebraska, 31-28IowaNo. 15Win at Illinois, 34-17Oregon and Ohio State jumped No. 15 Iowa in this week's third CFP rankings, clearing the Ducks' path to the playoff as the second team out, behind only Texas Tech. Iowa's 34-17 win at Illinois on Saturday came against the same team that swatted Oregon before the Ducks' current winning streak.That common opponent result could mean something this week in the updated rankings."I swear to God, I could care less about those guys (selection committee)," Iowa's Kirk Ferentz said Saturday. "They're going to do what they're going to do and I really don't care. Our goal was to come in here and win. It's not easy winning in college football, it's not easy winning on the road."The Hawkeyes have one less loss than Oregon this season, but selection committee chair Hunter Yurachek mentioned this week that the Ducks' and Buckeyes' body of work was more impressive."First of all, they kind of moved up to a point where we were going to compare the three of them collectively," Yurachek said. "You obviously have some head-to-head in that grouping where Oregon beat Ohio State, Ohio State beat Iowa, and Ohio State obviously had three losses. The strength of schedule for Oregon is nine. For Ohio State, 16. Iowa is 53."No. 16 Kentucky's path is cloudy coming off back-to-back losses and the Wildcats are underdogs at Missouri in Week 12. From preseason No. 1 to likely falling outside of the top-20 for a second time this season, this has been a campaign to forget for Ryan Day and the Buckeyes. Ohio State fell behind 14 points in the first half at Nebraska and 10 points in the fourth quarter before running out of time in Lincoln.The Buckeyes will finish the season next week against Michigan before likely heading to the Citrus Bowl to face an SEC opponent.Expected CFP movement BYU's less-than-impressive win at Kansas means the Cougars could get jumped on Tuesday night by Wake Forest. If the selection committee puts 12th-ranked Texas Tech in the same pod, the Red Raiders may move, too.Texas Tech beat Baylor, 20-10, and is one win away from getting back to the Big 12 Championship Game, likely against Utah. If Kansas had beaten BYU, Texas Tech could've clinched with a win in Waco, but now will have to beat TCU (Nov. 26) to get there.Ninth-ranked Tennessee escaped LSU inside Neyland Stadium, sending Lane Kiffin and the Tigers to their fifth loss. The Vols will move into first-round home game status after Indiana's loss at Washington and will be looking for style points next weekend against Vanderbilt.

title: 2026 Big Ten Championship Game scenarios as UCLA, Indiana losses create chaos entering regular-season finales - CBS Sports
description: The Bruins and Hoosiers just needed to win out to make it to Indy, but both lost Saturday to create chaos
body:
The Bruins and Hoosiers just needed to win out to make it to Indy, but both lost Saturday to create chaos
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:14 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Big Ten's terrible, no good, very bad year got a whole lot worse on Saturday when the only two teams in current position for a College Football Playoff berth lost on the road in overtime -- and threw the Big Ten title game picture into chaos in the process. Coming into this week, the formula for the Big Ten championship game was simple: if No. 4 UCLA and No. 8 Indiana won their last two games, they'd face each other in Indianapolis. The Bruins simply needed to go 1-1 against Michigan and USC to punch their ticket, but after the 3:30 p.m. ET window closed on Saturday, there's suddenly a four-team logjam for the two spots in Indianapolis. First, No. 8 Indiana got taken to overtime for a third time this season, but this time the Hoosiers couldn't escape in Seattle, hooking a game-tying field goal attempt wide left to give Washington a signature win this season. Shortly after, in Ann Arbor, No. 4 UCLA saw starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach get carted off after a big hit in the first overtime and, after trading field goals with Michigan, failed to convert on their first attempt in the two-point shootout in triple OT and watched as the Wolverines were successful in pulling out a massive 18-16 win. 
Big Ten standingsSchoolRecordWeek 13 opponentUCLA7-1USCOregon6-2WashingtonIndiana6-2PurdueIowa6-2NebraskaOnce again, UCLA controls its destiny heading into the final week, where a win gets them to Indianapolis. However, with more quarterback uncertainty and how much the offense struggled in overtime with third-stringer Madden Iamaleava inserted into the game, there is serious concern about the Bruins' ability to beat USC in the finale. A Bruins loss creates even more chaos, and all four teams have a path to the final Big Ten title game. Big Ten title game scenariosUCLA vs. OregonIf Oregon and UCLA both win on Saturday, they are headed to Indianapolis for a rematch of the game UCLA won earlier this year. UCLA has to beat USC with quarterback concerns, while the Ducks have to take down a Washington team that just beat Indiana. If that happens, UCLA grabs the top seed by being the only 1-loss team, and Oregon wins any tiebreaker with Iowa and Indiana based on record among common opponents. Oregon can get to 5-0 against common opponents of Indiana and Iowa with a win over Washington, while Iowa would be 4-1 if they beat Nebraska next week (loss to Ohio State) and Indiana is 3-2 (losses to Washington and Ohio State). The Ducks' win over Ohio State also wins them any two-way tiebreakers over Iowa and Indiana. Oregon vs. IowaIf Oregon wins and UCLA loses, then things get complicated. The first tiebreaker is common opponent; the lone common opponent between Oregon, Iowa, Indiana and UCLA is Michigan, which drops UCLA from contention. Then, in that same three-team scenario from above, Oregon takes the top seed, and Iowa takes the second seed based on the record against common opponents. UCLA vs. IndianaIf Oregon loses, it opens up the door for Indiana. UCLA faces the Hoosiers if the Hawkeyes also lose to Nebraska on Saturday and the Hoosiers beat Purdue -- who they will be heavily favored against. UCLA's result against USC would not matter in this scenario. That's the simplest path to a UCLA-Indiana game that many anticipated seeing coming into this week, but it would require a very different path to be taken. In the event Oregon loses and Iowa and Indiana both win, things get extremely complicated, but the tiebreakers would depend on whether UCLA wins. If UCLA loses to USC, that creates a new three-way tiebreaker that would go to Indiana based on common opponents. UCLA and Iowa would be tied in common opponent record, but the next tiebreaker is if Minnesota beats Wisconsin, the Gophers would have a better record than Michigan regardless of what happens in The Game, and UCLA would advance.Indiana vs. IowaIn the event of the above scenario, if Minnesota loses to Wisconsin and Michigan upsets Ohio State, then things get even more complicated and go to the "cumulative conference winning percentage of all conference opponents." We would not know whether UCLA or Iowa would win that until the results of next week are concluded, but there is a path to Iowa making it in via that tiebreaker, which would send them to Indy to face the Hoosiers. UCLA vs. IowaIowa gets to Indy against UCLA if the Bruins win, Purdue stuns Indiana, Iowa is able to beat Nebraska and Oregon loses. They also get there if the Bruins lose, Indiana loses and Oregon wins by way of a three-way tiebreaker with UCLA and Oregon. If Oregon loses, but UCLA, Indiana and Iowa all win, the Hawkeyes win the two-way tiebreaker with Indiana if Wisconsin also beats Minnesota. That collection of results would mean Washington would finish 5-4 after beating Oregon in conference play and the Gophers would be 4-5. Considering both lost to Ohio State, the next highest-finishing team would be Washington, who Iowa beat and Indiana lost to, sending the Hawkeyes to Indianapolis.

title: 2026 ACC Championship Game: Miami vs. Wake Forest rematch headlines final conference title matchup - CBS Sports
description: The ACC Championship Game era will conclude with Miami pursuing its first-ever ACC title
body:
The ACC Championship Game era will conclude with Miami pursuing its first-ever ACC title
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026 ACC Championship Game will carry historic significance with many conference championship games set to be taken off the calendar next season to make room for the expanded 24-team College Football Playoff. For the ACC, that means the end of an era that stretches back to 2005 when the league expanded to 12 teams and two divisions. There have been seven different winners across the 21 previous editions of the game, but not once has Miami been able to celebrate an ACC championship. Miami clinched its second-ever ACC Championship Game appearance with a win against Virginia Tech in Week 12, and now will get an opportunity to win the ACC for the first time. The Hurricanes joined the conference back in 2004, still in the afterglow of the program's fifth national championship, and their addition brought with it the expectations that "The U" would be a regular contender in this newly created title game. Twenty-two years later, Miami has the unique claim to being 3-1 in College Football Playoff games yet 0-1 in ACC Championship Games, and Mario Cristobal will be making his first appearance in the game after two years of falling just short with late-season losses and funky tiebreaker rules. Wake Forest also clinched its spot for the ACC Championship Game in Week 12, blowing out Georgia Tech in the same manner that the Demon Deacons have been dispatching most opponents here in the back half of the season. Jake Dickert's squad has beaten its last eight opponents (8-0) by an average of 37.4 points per game, and a rematch against Miami provides the stage to get even after the Hurricanes won 33-20 in Winston-Salem back in Week 3. Wake Forest, unlike Miami, does have an ACC championship in the title game era after winning back in 2006 in the second-ever edition of the game. The Demon Deacons played for the ACC championship again in 2021, falling to Pitt, and with this bid have now reached the ACC Championship Game three times with three different head coaches.    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    What to know about Miami The Hurricanes were expected to be here, getting the nod as an overwhelming favorite to win the league in the preseason after finishing as the national runner-up a year ago. And with an unbeaten record at the end of October, this Miami team appeared as though it could be carrying an argument as a top-two team in the country again when it showed up to Charlotte. But a loss at Notre Dame and the injury to star wide receiver Malachi Toney have shifted the outlook for Miami's edge in this matchup, even as the Hurricanes remain a popular pick to finish the year atop the league. 
Before Toney's injury, Miami scored 38 points or more in six of its first seven games but has not hit that mark in the three games since (2-1). The Hurricanes clinched their spot in the ACC Championship Game, rallying back from a 14-0 deficit at home against Virginia Tech for a 28-20 win. Still, even as Miami might be dealing with closer-than-expected margins and some injury issues coming down the stretch, it's still the most talented roster in the ACC, led by a coaching staff that just rolled through the CFP bracket a year ago. It's also led by Darian Mensah, who this year has been one of the top quarterbacks in the country. Mensah showed grit in a second-half comeback effort that ultimately fell short at Notre Dame, and the emergence of his former Duke teammate Cooper Barkate (who won the ACC Championship Game with Mensah last season) has helped backfill some of that receiving production that's been lost to injury. Miami's outlook in the College Football Playoff was out of its hands on championship weekend a year ago as they missed out on the conference title game due to the ACC's tiebreaker policy. Now Cristobal won't have to wonder how the selection committee will react to a re-racked set of rankings on that fateful Sunday morning in early December, because the Hurricanes get a chance to make a final statement on the committee this time and potentially seal their spot in the 12-team bracket. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    What to know about Wake Forest Jack Dickert exceeded his Year 1 expectations when he guided the Demon Deacons to nine wins in 2025, and it was the mistake of the preseason prognosticators to think that Wake Forest would regress to the pack in the ACC for Year 2. No, instead of winning at the margins as they did a year ago, the 2026 Demon Deacons have been leaving absolutely no doubt with their performance on the field. Boasting one of the largest point margins in the country and one of the best marks against the spread (both in terms of cover percentage and cover margin), the data backs up what our eyes have confirmed for weeks: Wake Forest has been playing like one of the best teams in the country. They are a deserved national title contender, and now will get a chance to play their way into the College Football Playoff with a spot secured in the ACC Championship Game. The offensive excellence starts with Gio Lopez, who arrived in Winston-Salem after an unsatisfying season at North Carolina but got to reunite with a familiar face in offensive coordinator Rob Ezell. Dickert hired Ezell from South Alabama after the Jags were led by Lopez in 2024, and getting the coordinator and quarterback back under the same roof has yielded positive results for both player and program. Wake Forest is among the nation's leaders in most major offensive categories, with wide receiver Carlos Hernandez performing at an All-American level as the X-factor skill player in the offense. Defensively, this is a group that has played some great complementary football, forcing turnovers and getting stops in high-leverage situations to help balance the explosiveness of the offense. This isn't the best defense in the country on a snap-by-snap basis, but they've rounded into a top-15 unit when it comes to points-per-drive allowed, which speaks to a bend-but-don't-break approach that's been clicking over the last couple of weeks.  
Miami vs. Wake Forest prediction These two teams have shown far different form than when they played in late September, and Wake Forest has been arguably operating at a higher and healthier level than the top-five Hurricanes. Jake Dickert's team has pounded all of its opponents since the Miami loss, putting up 38+ points in every game and beating opponents by one of the widest margins in the country. When you throw in Malachi Toney's injury, there's absolutely a chance to see Wake Forest even the score and claim the ACC championship, likely sending both teams into the 12-team College Football Playoff bracket. Prediction: Wake Forest wins the ACC championship.

title: Matt Rhule stumps for Jeremiah Smith's Heisman case after Nebraska's win over Ohio State - CBS Sports

College football's top wideout had another monster outing for the struggling Buckeyes

        As far as Nebraska coach Matt Rhule is concerned, Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith has already wrapped up college football's most prestigious individual honor this season.The record-setting Ohio State wideout was unstoppable during Saturday's 31-28 loss to the Huskers. He registered six catches for 165 yards and two touchdowns, including a 67-yarder on a gallop in the first half."Jeremiah Smith, give him the Heisman," Rhule said after the game surrounded by Nebraska fans at midfield. "I mean, we doubled him (throughout)."With his third straight 100-yard outing and seventh of the season, Smith now has 86 catches for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns, besting his freshman and sophomore numbers during a pair of All-American campaigns.
According to the latest Heisman odds via FanDuel Sportsbook updated Saturday afternoon, Smith is the frontrunner (-360) ahead of Miami quarterback Darian Mensah (+480), Utah signal caller Devon Dampier (+1200) and Wake Forest quarterback Gio Lopez (+2500)."I don't think I've ever competed against a player as talented and special -- and I've had a chance to play against a lot of them -- than that kid Jeremiah Smith," Rhule said during his presser. "That man, he is unbelievable, the way he can absolutely just tilt a game."Smith's last four performances have come without quarterback Julian Sayin, who the Buckeyes lost for the season earlier this fall during a win at Indiana to an arm injury. At times, freshman Luke Fahey has simply thrown in Smith's direction despite routine double and -- sometimes, triple -- coverage, and he's still coming down with the football.
The Buckeyes ran only 49 plays against the Huskers and were often beaten at the line of scrimmage."When you watch a game like this, you've got a lot of things that you have to change," Day said about potential personnel changes at season's end. "We don't have a choice. We've got to get this thing together next week to go win this game."Ohio State will play its final game of the regular season next week against Michigan, likely Smith's last time suiting up for the Buckeyes as a probable top-5 pick in April's NFL Draft.
"We're not gonna win many games if we're giving up 31 points and only getting two stops in the whole game," said Day, after dropping 5-6 in his last 11 contests at Ohio State against Power Four competition.

A devastating injury to Julian Sayin, fourth-quarter collapses and questionable staff moves derailed a national championship favorite and sparked the program's worst collapse since 2011
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026

    5:36 pm ET

        A season that started with national championship aspirations and a preseason No. 1 ranking could end with a trip to the Citrus Bowl.No. 14 Ohio State's faint playoff hopes were officially extinguished Saturday when Nebraska broke a decade-long losing streak and finally got a win over a top-25 opponent. Ecstatic Nebraska fans rushed the field to celebrate the Cornhuskers' 31-28 win over the Buckeyes.It is the first time since 2011 that Ohio State has lost consecutive road games. In case you forgot, 2011 was the Luke Fickell interim 6-6 season that preceded the Urban Meyer era. It's not a stretch to say this 2026 season is the worst in 15 years, and one could argue it's even worse than 2011 given the expectations and talent on the roster. Poor Jeremiah Smith's talent is being wasted on the most disappointing Ohio State team in decades. How did Ohio State get here? Here's a look at the Buckeyes' drop to rock bottom. 
Winter 2026Ryan Day made two key decisions last winter that had the potential to significantly impact the Buckeyes' season.First, Day hired former Atlanta Falcons head coach Arthur Smith as his offensive coordinator. On paper, it felt like a potential upgrade over the outgoing Brian Hartline, who left to become South Florida's head coach. Under Hartline, Ohio State's offense was efficient but seemed to be missing some of the explosiveness from the previous season. Day even took over play-calling responsibilities late in the season when Hartline was balancing two jobs. Smith, who had been the Pittsburgh Steelers' offensive coordinator the previous season, was expected to improve the run game.Next, Ohio State retained defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, who had received some interest in returning to the NFL. Ohio State's defense flourished in Year 1 with Patricia, finishing No. 1 in total defense and scoring defense (only 9.3 points allowed per game). Ohio State rewarded Patricia, making him the highest-paid assistant coach in college football. 
Collapse in AustinOhio State led No. 4 Texas, 23-3, in the fourth quarter and … lost.It was a historic collapse for the Buckeyes on Sept. 12 in Austin. Texas' fourth-quarter comeback to win 24-23 was the largest against a No. 1-ranked team in history. It had the potential to be the kind of marquee win that Ohio State could hold up if anyone attacked its playoff resume. To beat a playoff-caliber team like Texas on the road would have been ginormous. Instead, it was a what-could-have-been result that elicited early questions about Arthur Smith after Ohio State's late-game conservative play-calling blew up in its face. Still, it felt too early to panic about a team that was considered to be one of, if not the, most talented teams in the country. As long as Ohio State took care of business in Big Ten play, it'd be fine. 
Won the battle, lost the war The definition of a pyrrhic victory for the Buckeyes. Ohio State held off Indiana, 19-15, on Oct. 17 in a rematch of last year's Big Ten Championship Game. It gave Ohio State a resume-defining win, but the bigger news was the injury star quarterback Julian Sayin suffered late in the game. Sayin fractured his right elbow, according to reports, and was later ruled out indefinitely. Ohio State would never recover from the loss of Sayin, a Heisman Trophy finalist in 2025, and didn't have a viable backup option to keep the offense humming. Sayin never got the credit he deserved as Ohio State's quarterback, as critics believed he was more a product of the surrounding talent than what he could do himself. And while there's no question having Jeremiah Smith to throw the ball to downfield was supremely helpful, the impact of Sayin's absence should make fans realize how good they had it. No treat against TrojansIt was a Halloween debacle for the Buckeyes against a desperate USC team looking for a big win. It was the first real test of how Ohio State would look without Sayin, and the Buckeyes failed. 
True freshman Luke Fahey wasn't bad against the Trojans, but the offense clearly took a step back. In its 30-18 loss to USC, Ohio State ended up with three field goals on its first five offensive drives despite having the ball on the Trojans' 1-yard line on one of those drives. Perhaps even more concerning was how bad the defense looked at times. USC capitalized on a defensive breakdown for a 69-yard touchdown in the first minute of the game. By the middle of the third quarter, USC had a 27-9 lead it would never relinquish. It would be too simplistic  -- and perhaps unfair -- to say that the defense stopped playing as well because it didn't believe in Fahey the way it did Sayin, but it is strange how much worse Matt Patricia's group seemed to look, from an effort and execution standpoint, post-Sayin injury. There was hope that Ohio State had enough talent to survive the loss of Sayin. The poor effort against USC cast a lot of doubt on that. 
Fake punt breaks OSUOregon's gutsy (and successful) fake punt call in the second quarter seemed to break an Ohio State team that had raced out to a 14-0 lead.It was stunning to see Ohio State just completely collapse afterward in what turned into a 41-28 loss to the Ducks that severely damaged the Buckeyes' playoff hopes. This was the last-stand type of game for Ohio State, a must-win home game against a team that had also lost its own star quarterback (Dante Moore) to an injury this season. And for a quarter-and-a-half, Ohio State looked the part. But in what has proven to be a defining characteristic of this Ohio State team, when it faces real adversity, it crumbles. It happened against Texas, and it happened again against Oregon. At one point, Oregon scored 38 consecutive points, the first time since 1999 the Buckeyes gave up that many points in a row. 
"We didn't expect any of this to happen," Day said. The loss prompted a series of questions, from possible staff changes to why Ohio State hasn't been better at developing quarterbacks. Most importantly, all the goodwill Ryan Day collected from the 2024 title run seemed to dissipate with the loss. Disaster seasonSome of us, including this College Football Playoff prognosticator, already thought Ohio State's playoff hopes should be dead. But after a win over Northwestern and chaos engulfing the teams ranked above them, the Buckeyes moved all the way up to No. 14 in this week's CFP Rankings. It was still a long shot, but one couldn't definitively rule Ohio State out in case a few of the higher-ranked teams lost in the final weeks of the season.Nebraska ended that notion once and for all. The Cornhuskers ended a 31-game losing streak against ranked opponents when they beat the Buckeyes. The loss drops Ohio State to 7-4, its worst record since 2011. Ryan Day is now 7-6 in his last 13 games as Ohio State's head coach. 
The defense again struggled, especially early as Nebraska built a 21-7 lead. When it badly needed a stop late in the game, it could not stop Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea from getting the first down. Colandrea finished with four total touchdowns (3 passing, 1 rushing) and delivered the final nail in the coffin for Ohio State's season."We're not gonna win many games if we're giving up 31 points and only getting two stops in the whole game," Day said afterward. As bleak as it felt for Day and Ohio State after a shocking 2024 loss to Michigan, this is worse. And it has the potential to get even uglier if Ohio State can't beat a bad Michigan team next week in The Game.

title: Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him - CBS Sports
description: Curry isn't going to win the award for a number of reasons, but his absence is speaking volumes right now
body:
Curry isn't going to win the award for a number of reasons, but his absence is speaking volumes right now
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books. So it's really saying something to start registering all-time marks of franchise ineptitude, which is precisely what the Warriors have done over the last week. After battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history. The only other time this has happened to a Warriors team was in February of 1998, a few months after Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo. The total margin of that four-game losing streak was 104 points. This current one is even worse. These Warriors have lost their last four by 109 points, and what makes it even more jarring is comparing them to the team that had won eight straight prior to Curry's injury. That 1997-98 team was trash all year, starting 1-14 and finishing with just 19 wins without ever winning more than three straight games. These Warriors, on the other hand, were starting to look like a legitimate playoff-caliber team. A cynic would say that run of victories came against a softer schedule than what they have faced of late, but that qualification doesn't hold much, if any, water. That eight-game run included wins over the Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat and an Orlando Magic team that has immediately gone on to win five of its last six. 

        
            
                NBA Power Rankings: The LaMelo Ball effect is being felt in two places; Lakers take top spot from Spurs
                
                    Brad Botkin                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Perhaps the Warriors would have lost to the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs even with Curry. Hell, maybe they would've lost to the New Orleans Pelicans, Dallas Mavericks and Memphis Grizzlies, too. That feels unlikely, but who knows? Even with Curry, the Warriors aren't good enough to start checking off scheduled wins. But that's not the point. The point is how utterly incapable they have looked in losing these games. Not only have they lost each of these last four by at least 20 points, but they've also been held under 100 points in all of them. That's a combination of incompetence that stretches beyond a franchise mark. That hasn't happened to a single other team this century. Is Curry's absence his strongest MVP case?Before we try to answer that, let's just agree upfront that Curry has little to no chance of actually winning what would be his third MVP. The Warriors almost certainly won't have a good enough record to put him in real contention. His across-the-board counting stats, even if he were to maintain his torrid early pace, are not going to match those of Luka Dončić or Victor Wembanyama. 
The only real chance would be if both of those guys, and likely a bunch of others, failed to meet the 65-game threshold, but the chances of Curry, who has already missed six games and isn't expected to be re-evaluated until around Thanksgiving, making it to 65 games himself already feel next to impossible. He may be past the maximum 17 games-missed mark before he even returns from this injury. Which is to say, what we're asking here is whether Curry, at 38 years old and in his 18th season, is still the most valuable player in the league (has he always been?), not whether he'll actually win the award, and the answer to that question, at least in its simplest form, could very well lie in his absence. Just look at this team without him. Tale of two teamsORTGNRTGEFG%TS%Eight-game win streak with Curry122.2 (1st)+16.4 (1st)60.1 (1st)64.0 (1st)Four-game losing streak without Curry95.1 (30th)-27.4 (30th)43.4 (30th)48.1 (30th)Admittedly, there's some cherry-picking in those numbers. Curry actually didn't play in one of the wins during that eight-game streak, and the Warriors still beat the Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with a 122.8 offensive rating behind 37 points from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. We're also leaving out the aforementioned game against the Rockets on Nov. 11 in which Curry only played six minutes and the Warriors looked fine, or even good, in testing one of the best teams in the league to its limit. It also must be noted that Golden State lost its first three games of the season and looked every bit like the team many of us predicted would stink, all of which Curry played in. Still, the general rule applies. The Warriors go as Curry goes. That was true even in the golden years when the on/off splits, even with the likes of Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson still out there, always pointed to Curry as the clear MVP. "If I didn't have Steph, I would've been like every other NBA coach and lasted a few years [with the Warriors] and then gone and coached somewhere else," Steve Kerr has said, openly admitting that Curry, and Curry alone, has been the difference between a journeyman coaching career and a Hall-of-Fame one. He's not lying. Have a look at the numbers. 2014-presentOverall RecordWin PercentageKerr with Curry528-21870.6%Kerr without Curry88-14238.3%Even if you want to remove the 2019-20 season from the equation, when Durant had defected, Thompson missed the whole year and Curry only played in five games, Kerr is still a below-.500 coach at 74-96 without Curry in the lineup. This is a coach who has had all kinds of great players at his disposal over the years, and still it was always Curry in control of his and the organization's ultimate fate. This is still the case for the Warriors, who continue to fall off a cliff without Curry. When he's been on the floor this year, they have registered a 59.6 eFG%, which would rank first in the league. When he's off, they fall to 49.1%, which would rank last. Even the defensive decline we see in Curry's on/off splits can largely be tied back to his offense. Without him, the Warriors are unable to create the same shots and, when their new brand of shots miss far more often, they end up defending in transition on almost 3% more possessions. That's a big deal. It's meant almost five more points per game surrendered to fast breaks over this stretch. The Warriors have produced an average offensive rating of 103.8 in games Curry hasn't played this year, which would rank as the second-worst mark in the league. All told, they are 26.3 points per 100 possessions better in Curry's minutes this season, per Cleaning The Glass. By comparison, the Lakers drop by 25.5 points per 100 when Dončić sits. Wembanyama is in his own galaxy with this stat, representing a 37.8-point decline in San Antonio when he's off the floor. It's fair to say Wembanyama means as much to San Antonio's defense, where most of that decline happens, as Curry does to Golden State's offense, and certainly the Lakers falling off by as much as they do offensively, even with Austin Reaves as a legit secondary star, tells you everything you need to know about his impact. All of these guys are MVP players. But only one, by subjective definition, can be the most valuable, and the simple truth is the Lakers and Spurs are outfitted with far more functional rosters independent of their respective superstars. In Golden State, there is just nowhere else to turn. Nobody to generate any kind of consistent offensive leverage. No gravity. No shot creation. 
After the Warriors took that 38-point beating against the Spurs without Curry, the rookie Lendeborg, who had, in total unfairness, been saddled with filling Curry's go-to-scorer shoes, said "it felt helpless out there," and that is exactly what it has looked like since the Curry variable was removed from Golden State's equation. 
        
            
                Yaxel Lendeborg, Warriors get a taste of life without Stephen Curry: 'It felt helpless out there'
                
                    Brad Botkin                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
To be fair, the absence of a player is an imperfect lens through which to view value for a bunch of contextual reasons, not the least of which is how a team like Golden State is designed to play -- a specific, Curry-centric ecosystem not particularly amenable to abrupt adjustments. These players are not as bad as they have looked without Curry over these last four games. But by the same token, they aren't close to as good as they looked with Curry, either. I always laugh when my dad calls me saying things like, "This Pat Spencer guy can play!" Everyone looks like they can play next to Curry. And then he goes away and suddenly you're wondering how the hell this guy made the Washington Generals look like one of the best teams in the league. Is he some kind of miracle worker? 
In a basketball sense, that's not far off. Curry's individual production is already virtually unmatched, but it's his exponential powers, his ability to compound the returns of those around him, that set him apart. It's early, yes. Perhaps the Warriors will figure things out the longer Curry is away. Probably not. But maybe they at least can return to competitive functionality. Until then, however, it's pretty hard to not think Curry is the most valuable player in the league when you watch the Warriors play without him.

title: MLB rumors: Logan Webb trade possible for Giants, Freddy Peralta market picking up steam, more - CBS Sports

Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Saturday, Nov. 21

        The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Logan Webb trade a possibility for Giants
Will the San Francisco Giants trade their ace this offseason? That's a reasonable question to ask now that FanSided is reporting that the Giants are open to trade discussions regarding veteran right-hander Logan Webb. No doubt, Webb would be a coveted presence on the offseason market. Webb, who just recently turned 30, endured a bit of a down 2026 on the run-prevention front, but the overall body of work remains very strong. For his career, the three-time All-Star has a career ERA+ of 115 with three top-10 finishes in the American League Cy Young vote. In three of the past four seasons, he's topped 200 innings. 
Webb is under contract through 2028, and that extra year of team control makes him even more of an alluring trade target for contenders in need of rotation upgrades. Freddy Peralta market picking up steam
Freddy Peralta, who'll be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is one of the strongest free-agent starting pitchers on the market not named Tarik Skubal. As such, there's healthy interest in his services. The Tampa Bay Rays, the Chicago White Sox, the San Diego Padres, the Toronto Blue Jays, and two presently unknown clubs all have significant interest in signing Peralta, the Athletic reports. Peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the New York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form. 
Itoh visits ChicagoRight-hander Hiromi Itoh, who's seeking to make the leap from Japan to MLB, was recently in Chicago to visit the Cubs or the White Sox, ESPN reports. Both Windy City squads are in need of pitching help, and Itoh would certainly help them on that front. The 29-year-old Itoh ranked 26th on CBS Sports' offseason list of the top free agents in the current class. Here's part of our write-up: "A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon Ham Fighters are expected to post Itoh, who turned 29 in August, this winter."The Cubs have a lot of uncertainty in the rotation, while the White Sox still need help even after adding Dustin May this offseason. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mets getting calls on Vientos
The New York Mets retained the services of first baseman Mark Vientos leading up to the recent non-tender deadline despite his pattern of decline over the last two seasons. Now, Vientos could be on the move. The soon-to-be 27-year-old has been the subject of trade inquiries, The Athletic reports. 
While Vientos is coming off a highly disappointing 2026 season, he still has power potential and in his semi-recent past a 2024 campaign in which he hit 27 home runs in 111 games. All of that makes Vientos a fairly compelling change-of-scenery possibility, and the Mets may seek to make that happen this winter.

title: Leeds expose Chelsea's unresolved defensive problems as Xabi Alonso's crew yet to find footing - CBS Sports
description: A 4-1 home loss to Leeds laid bare the persistent defensive cracks and tactical chaos that Xabi Alonso has so far
body:
A 4-1 home loss to Leeds laid bare the persistent defensive cracks and tactical chaos that Xabi Alonso has so far failed to fix at Stamford Bridge
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LONDON -- This was supposed to be the year, the time when Chelsea grew up and a proper manager started extracting consistent performances from a squad whose much-vaunted talent is too rarely expressed in results form. In this most in-flux of Premier League seasons, Xabi Alonso still might leave her with something. It is not going to take particular excellence for a club like this to achieve the bare minimum of Champions League qualification. Adequacy might do it.Once more, however, that is threatening to be a standard beyond Chelsea. This 4-1 defeat at home to old rivals Leeds has them squeezed into the Premier League's middle ground, those above them very visible proof of how much more can be done with less. There is nothing false about that position. Since the last weeks of summer, Alonso's team have given up so much at the back that their likeliest route to success seemed to be supernova seasons from all three of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Nothing else would paper over the cracks in the defense.And Alonso has tried a lot. Right backs in midfield, center backs as nominal left wing backs that are actually auxiliary central midfielders, switching the right wing back to center forward: in isolation, you could make a case for so many of these adjustments. When the performances are so inconsistent, why not change the XI every game? Alonso's success at Bayer Leverkusen, coupled with the inquisitive footballing mind that made the player so beloved of elite coaches, have earned him the right to experiment. Every change, however, begs the question of what the foundations underlying all this are. Those ought to have shone through this afternoon. Alonso's was as straightforward an XI as he has named. Estevao, Palmer and Rogers off an orthodox center forward, Moises Caicedo running the double pivot and an orthodox back four in front of Emiliano Martinez. This looked like a team intent on playing its way.

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Instead, they had Leeds' game foisted upon them. That might have been different if they had not lost Caicedo. He seemed to have a handle on the game before colliding with James Justin as both competed for a high ball. Those often seemed like the only sort up for grabs today; even when Chelsea played well, they were playing the sort of game Leeds wanted. This wasn't quite the rapid attacking up the gut with which Xabi Alonso charmed the Premier League early in this season. It was bypass the press-ball, get it straight up to the final third and see what comes of it.It can work. Justin, exemplary as a man-marker without the ball and roving agent of chaos in the Chelsea half, cleared a goal kick straight into the back of Morgan Rogers. He moved swiftly up the Leeds gut, his pass to Emmanuel Emegha delivered at just the right moment for the Premier League debutant to slam in the opener. It was perhaps the only moment of clinical execution from the Blues.They needed so many more. After all, this is a team that fails to meet the standards in so many aspects of defending. They press like a newly promoted team. They always seem to name one defender who can be picked on in the duels (starting left back Pep Charravia ranks 101st of 102 defenders for duel success over 300-plus Premier League minutes). Midfielders routinely abandon runners. When Caicedo left this game the feint thread holding the team together was cut.
No one had the composure to deal with the bouncing ball moments after Emegha's opener, Noah Okafor free to move into the box and shoot low through a crowd of legs. No one seemed truly live to the danger for Okafor's second, thundered into the roof of the net when Chelsea could not repel pressure down their right. Between that a contentious penalty, Jayden Bogle's long-range effort striking Rogers right in the grey area between sleeve and arm. If that hadn't been the moment when Chelsea caved, another would have come along."Leeds believed more than us," Alonso admitted. "We didn't show a good enough reaction." The quick one-two punch had been more than enough to send Chelsea heads to the floor. A two-goal deficit ought not to be beyond their reach, but the final 32 minutes saw them outshot seven to six with fewer passes completed into the penalty area. Palmer's most notable action of this game was to row with Joao Pedro as he made his way down the tunnel. Nothing he could have done would have overcome the problems Chelsea made for themselves at the other end. It really wouldn't hurt, though if he did more than nothing.
These feel like problems unresolved by a manager who was supposed to be the savior. Eleven Premier League games is not a lot to turn the tide but it is enough to give us a sense of who this team are. The answer is a team whose early scoring streak covered for a below-average attack (1.25 non-penalty expected goals per game, 14th in the Premier League) and a below-average defense (1.44 non-penalty expected goals allowed per game, 15th in the Premier League). The game state-warping impact of scoring with your first shot can only mitigate so much.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Is it time for a conversation about Alonso and pressure? If so it has to be caveated by the unity and purpose he fostered at Bayer Leverkusen, qualities this dressing room sorely needs. He might not have corralled the superstars at Real Madrid but the press and possession system he forged could have achieved great things given time. Stitching together a version of this Chelsea, overloaded with number 10s and underpowered defensive players, that suits the more direct and chaotic Premier League was always going to be a coaching challenge.And of course this is not the Roman Abramovich era. Swapping out coaches is not a silver bullet for perennial trophy contenders but instead the modus operandi of an ownership group that are the most serious problem at Stamford Bridge. Someone is going to have to be afforded time to corral this squad or indeed tear it down and start again. Doing that is going to be a club-wide effort, including fans. Few of them hung around to wave off a side who had allowed old rivals Leeds a first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999, the same side who had let Tottenham break the habit of a lifetime last month.
The vibes are bad. The performances might be worse. This brand new start is feeling all too familiar.

Saturday's action in Doha provided plenty of interesting talking points heading toward the end of the year
